Prevention: Field sanitation, remove weeds and fallen leaves in the field
Proper ventilation to reduce humidity in the green house
Use a less soluble form of nitrogen and apply it in small portions throughout the season rather than all at once.
Slow-release fertilizers such as organic fertilizers or urea-based time-release formulations are best
Monitoring: Monitoring should be carried out after transplanting, look out for ants as they are often associated with aphid populations.
Large numbers of ants climbing plants often indicates aphids or other honeydew-producing insects that might be on limbs and leaves
Check blade back for aphids in mid-late
When occurs sporadically in the field, direct control should be carried out
Direct Control: Luring and killing aphids using yellow boards
Restrictions: Chemical pesticides must be applied strictly according to the prescribed dosages to avoid residue problems
Rotational application of pesticides to avoid resistance
PPEs should be worn when dealing with chemical pesticides
